headline: Protein language and geometric models predict enzyme kinetics and mutation pathogenicity
label: Protein Language Model Prediction
summary: Zero-shot enzyme discovery from protein language models arrives alongside leakage-controlled and additive-baseline benchmarking of reported gains.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep representation learning on protein sequences and structures, with growing scrutiny of whether reported performance reflects genuine learning. PLM-clust applies k-means over protein language model embeddings with zero-shot scoring to recursively discover glycosyl hydrolase enzymes. O2DENet and PIMetaKcat address enzyme kinetic parameter prediction under out-of-distribution and few-shot conditions, with PIMetaKcat adding Arrhenius constraints for temperature-dependent kcat. Geometry-aware methods extend this to generation and design: GeomMotif benchmarks motif preservation using scRMSD and pLDDT, Surleton jointly models backbone and surface geometry for inverse folding, and PROTEUS derives a zero-shot conformational plasticity score from SimpleFold embeddings. Skeptical benchmarking appears in MULTI-evolve, whose multimutant predictions track an additive model, and in Aiki-XP's leakage control. What is new is zero-shot enzyme discovery and zero-shot conformational scoring, alongside explicit tests of epistasis and leakage.
